- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) and forecast is below recent high, model tends to underreact — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.33) and forecast is above 70, model overestimates — cap forecast at 72–73 unless strong bullish sentiment persists.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to anticipate reversal — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in next 2–3 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model consistently underestimates late-period price peaks — increase final 5–7 days by 1–2% of average recent volatility.
- If sentiment history shows no recent bullish signals (all 0.00), model tends to be overly conservative — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to avoid “flat” forecast traps.
